title: Vector scoring pipeline visibility and per-route cost attribution
creator: Marco Ruiz
description: Add end-to-end visibility for the embedding -> reranking (vector scoring) pipeline with per-route dashboards, correlated traces, and token-level cost attribution. This ticket scopes the telemetry model, dashboard surface, alerting rules, and a lightweight tracing propagation mechanism so product teams can answer latency regressions, cost spikes, and quality regressions by route/model/tenant.
rationale: We frequently see customer tickets that say 'rerank suddenly got slow' or 'my bill jumped' but lack the signal to determine whether the regression is due to embedding model change, batching behavior, KV cache miss rates, or reranker kernel selection. Current metrics are too coarse (service-wide) and do not correlate traces to cost. Improving per-route observability reduces MTTI and allows targeted optimizations (batching, cache policies, model variant routing).
approach: 1) Add lightweight trace/span tags on the client-facing request and propagate through the embed call, cache lookup, and vector scoring stages. 2) Emit per-request cost tags (model, tokens_out, tokens_in, GPU-ms estimate, cache_hit boolean). 3) Create per-route dashboard templates in Console with P50/P95/P99 latency, cost-per-call, cache hit rate, batch-size distribution, and trace sample links. 4) Add alerting rules for sustained cost deviation and latency SLO breaches. 5) Roll through a staged canary enabling 100% trace sampling for 2 routes, 1% sampling everywhere else.
acceptance_criteria: Trace IDs are attached to every vector scoring request and appear in Console trace viewer with stage annotations
Dashboard template exists and can be instantiated per route with <24h rollup and 7d retention
Cost attribution shows per-route cost breakdown (embeddings compute, reranker compute, IO) for synthetic workload within +/-10% of billing estimator
Alerting rules fire on: p95 latency > SLO for 10m, per-route 3x cost anomaly over baseline for 15m, cache miss rate > 30% for 5m
Load test (1000 rps synthetic) demonstrates dashboards remain usable and tracing sampling does not exceed budgeted telemetry egress limits
updates: 2026-01-28: Ticket created after post-mortem for incident INC-2026-01-25 where rerank latency increased for 'search-pro' routes.
2026-02-03: Spike analysis prototype instrumented in staging. Added span tags: request.route_id, model.tags, batch.size, cache.hits.

2026-02-12: Design review with Console team — agreed on dashboard widgets: stacked waterfall for latency (embed, cache, score), histogram for batch sizes, cost waterfall for compute vs cache vs network.
2026-02-20: Security reviewed trace tags; no user PII allowed. Confirmed route_id is stable but not human-identifying.
2026-03-02: Implemented cost-estimator exporter for GPU-ms using kernel timing counters (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4187).
2026-03-10: Canary launched for routes: 'search-pro' and 'semantic-match' with 100% trace sampling; 1% sampling elsewhere. No SLO violations observed.
rollout_plan: Phase 2 (canary): Enable 100% sampling on two high-traffic routes and validate metrics (1 week)
Phase 3 (prod): Low-sampling default across all routes + per-route opt-in, create runbook and alerts (2 weeks)
Phase 4: Post-rollout evaluation and follow-ups (hotspots, cost-ops)
risks: High cardinality in traces if we attach unbounded route metadata — mitigated by route_id hashing and tag blacklists
Telemetry egress increase causing cost overruns — mitigated by sampling strategy and aggregated rollups
Cost estimator mismatches vs billing — validate with small customer invoices before wide release
qa_steps: Run synthetic suite: vary batch sizes and ensure histogram and waterfall charts reflect change
Inject cache miss pattern and verify alert triggers and trace highlights cache_lookup spans
Run cost smoke test: benchmark GPU-ms estimator against kernel timers and confirm within 10%
Validate anonymization: no PII in traces or tags
Test rollbacks: ensure disabling sampling removes extra telemetry in <5 minutes
notes: Design decision: prefer a coarse-grained cost estimator over per-token metering to avoid adding per-token network overhead.
Follow-up: surface model-variant breakdown (quantized vs fp16) in a later card depending on pilot results.
Related: coordinate with Billing team for reconciliation for first customer pilots.
